executiveSummary: Analysis of 20 surveillance reports spanning November 2025 to May 2026 from ECDC and PAHO reveals multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1), a BSL-3 select agent, has generated repeated epidemiological updates in the Americas region, indicating sustained zoonotic transmission risk with pandemic potential. The Southern Hemisphere influenza season is commencing simultaneously with ongoing mpox transmission in the Americas, creating compounded respiratory and viral threat burdens. Additional concerns include yellow fever activity, dengue surges, measles resurgence, and rising pertussis incidence across the Americas region.
bottomLine: Multiple overlapping biological threats including the BSL-3 select agent H5N1 avian influenza, yellow fever, and mpox require heightened surveillance and coordinated response across the Americas and Europe.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained circulation
Repeated PAHO alerts suggest ongoing zoonotic spillover events in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential and high case fatality rate in humans
Dual reporting periods suggest no containment between late 2025 and early 2026
threats.action: Activate enhanced zoonotic surveillance protocols, strengthen human-animal interface monitoring, ensure antiviral stockpile readiness, and coordinate with FAO and OIE on affected animal populations

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active transmission
Yellow fever is a BSL-3 select agent with hemorrhagic fever potential
Alert suggests cases occurring outside historically endemic zones or with increased intensity
Vaccination coverage gaps may be contributing to outbreak risk
threats.action: Verify vaccination coverage in affected and border regions, issue travel health advisories, deploy emergency vaccine reserves if needed, and enhance vector surveillance for Aedes and Haemagogus mosquitoes

threats.name: Mpox
signals: Epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating continued transmission in the Americas
Mpox virus is a BSL-3 select agent requiring enhanced biosafety measures
Sustained circulation following 2022-2024 global outbreak suggests endemic establishment risk
Multiple clade variants may be co-circulating
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing, ensure JYNNEOS vaccine availability for high-risk populations, implement infection control guidance, and monitor for clade divergence

threats.name: Dengue
signals: Epidemiological update issued February 2026 amid historically high dengue burden in the Americas
Record-breaking dengue seasons in prior years suggest continued amplified transmission
Multiple serotype co-circulation increases risk of severe dengue
Vector control challenges in urban settings across Latin America
threats.action: Intensify integrated vector management programs, strengthen hospital surge capacity for severe dengue, enhance serotype surveillance, and issue public communications on personal protection

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza - Southern Hemisphere Season Onset
signals: PAHO alert issued April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
Simultaneous circulation with RSV flagged in January 2026 alert indicating dual respiratory burden
Influenza and RSV co-circulation can overwhelm healthcare capacity
Multiple ECDC weekly threat reports across Weeks 16-20 suggest Northern Hemisphere activity continuing
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake in Southern Hemisphere countries, prepare healthcare systems for increased respiratory illness burden, monitor for novel influenza variants, and coordinate cross-hemisphere strain surveillance

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active measles transmission
Americas region had achieved elimination status making re-emergence especially concerning
Vaccination coverage gaps likely contributing to resurgence
Risk of spread across borders in region with high population movement
threats.action: Conduct emergency vaccination campaigns targeting under-vaccinated communities, strengthen case-based surveillance, verify import-linked chains of transmission, and coordinate with national immunization programs

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two epidemiological updates issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated incidence
Resurgence consistent with global pertussis rebound post-COVID pandemic
Waning immunity in adolescents and adults contributing to transmission
Infants remain at highest risk for severe disease and mortality
threats.action: Strengthen Tdap booster programs for adolescents and adults, ensure maternal pertussis vaccination, improve laboratory diagnostic capacity, and investigate potential antimicrobial resistance in circulating strains

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 2025 indicating cases in the Americas
Hantavirus pulmonary syndrome carries high case fatality rate of 35-50%
Rodent reservoir activity and human encroachment into endemic areas drives risk
Person-to-person transmission documented for Andes virus strain
threats.action: Enhance rodent control programs in endemic areas, issue public guidance on avoiding rodent contact, strengthen clinical recognition and supportive care capacity, and investigate potential person-to-person transmission clusters

selectAgentSummary: Three BSL-3 select agents have been detected or are actively circulating in the surveillance period. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) generated two separate PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026), indicating persistent zoonotic threat with pandemic potential in the Americas. Yellow Fever virus prompted a PAHO epidemiological alert in March 2026, suggesting active transmission in the Americas with risk to unvaccinated populations. Monkeypox virus (MPXV), a BSL-3 pathogen, continues circulating in the Americas as documented in an April 2026 PAHO update. All three detections require enhanced biosafety protocols, specialized laboratory handling, and coordinated international response measures.
amrSignals: Pertussis resurgence with two epidemiological updates within three months may warrant investigation of macrolide resistance in Bordetella pertussis isolates circulating in the Americas
GLP-1 receptor agonist misuse alert (Report 12) may indicate counterfeit pharmaceutical supply chains, indirectly increasing infection risk through unsafe injection practices
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen burden in the Americas region suggests potential healthcare system strain with H5N1, dengue, measles, pertussis, mpox, and yellow fever co-circulating
Post-pandemic immunity gaps are driving resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases including measles and pertussis across the Americas
Back-to-back PAHO H5N1 updates in November 2025 and March 2026 suggest that initial containment efforts were insufficient and zoonotic spillover risk remains unresolved
Southern Hemisphere influenza season onset coinciding with ongoing RSV circulation creates a compound respiratory threat window for healthcare systems
Chikungunya alert in February 2026 alongside dengue activity suggests active Aedes aegypti vector pressure across multiple arboviral diseases simultaneously
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly threat reports (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) indicates a sustained elevated threat environment in Europe during spring 2026
